renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: mutation_matrix
  title: Mutation matrix
  description: |-
    Each cell is a sample and a gene, coloured by the type of mutation observed there. It answers which genes are mutated in which samples and how the mutation types are distributed.
    How to read: a row full of cells is a gene mutated across many samples, which can mark a lineage-defining change or a hotspot. A column full of cells is a divergent sample. Rows are ordered by how often the gene is mutated.
  kind: oncoplot
  config:
    legend_position: bottom
  roles:
    sample_id: sample_id
    gene: gene
    mutation_type: mutation_type

- component: card
  title: Samples with mutations
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct samples with at least one observed mutation, with the number of sample and gene combinations beside it, and the bars rank the genes with the most mutations. It answers how widespread the mutations are and where they concentrate.
    How to read: a gene that leads the ranking is a hotspot or a lineage marker. Open the mutation matrix to see which samples carry it.
  column: sample_id
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: gene
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: mutations, by gene

- component: card
  title: Genes with mutations
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct genes carrying a mutation, and the bars rank the mutation types by the number of genes they touch. It answers which kinds of change are the most widespread across the genome.
    How to read: a ranking led by synonymous changes means mostly silent variation. Many stop-gained or frameshift changes in a gene deserve a look at the variant table.
  column: gene
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: mutation_type
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: genes, by mutation type

- component: table
  title: Mutation table
  description: |-
    One row is one sample, gene and mutation type combination, with its mutation label. It answers which changes sit behind each cell of the matrix.
    How to read: Sort by gene to see which samples carry a change in it, or by sample to list all of its changes. Look for genes that recur across samples and for rare mutation types. It complements the matrix tile of the same output, which shows the same cells as a grid.

- component: card
  title: Mutations by type
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of observed mutations, with the number of distinct genes beside it, and the bar splits the mutations by type. It answers what the mix of changes looks like.
    How to read: a bar dominated by synonymous changes means mostly silent variation. A visible share of stop-gained or frameshift changes points at changes that can disable a protein.
  column: gene
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: mutation_type
  caption: mutations, by type

- component: advanced_viz
  id: lollipop
  title: Variants along each gene
  description: |-
    Each lollipop is a variant placed at its genome position within a gene, coloured by its predicted effect and sized by its allele frequency. It answers where the variants fall in each gene and which of them change the protein.
    How to read: clusters of non-synonymous or stop-gained changes in one gene suggest a region under selection or a problem region. Large heads are variants present in most reads, small heads are minor variants. Hover a head or open the table tile to read the change.
  kind: lollipop
  config:
    top_n_labels: 5
  roles:
    feature_id: GENE
    position: POS
    category: EFFECT
    effect: AF
    label: mutation_label

- component: advanced_viz
  id: oncoplot
  title: Mutation matrix
  description: |-
    Each cell is a sample and a gene, coloured by the predicted effect of the variant there. It answers which genes are mutated in which samples.
    How to read: a row full of cells is a gene mutated across many samples, such as a lineage marker. A column full of cells is a divergent sample. Rows are ordered by how often the gene is mutated.
  kind: oncoplot
  config:
    legend_position: bottom
  roles:
    sample_id: sample
    gene: GENE
    mutation_type: EFFECT

- component: advanced_viz
  id: manhattan
  title: Allele frequency along the genome
  description: |-
    Each point is a variant at its genome position, with its allele frequency on the vertical axis, coloured by its predicted effect. It answers where along the genome variants sit and how many are fixed rather than minor.
    How to read: points at the top are present in most reads and form the consensus changes, while points near the bottom are minor variants. A band of points at intermediate frequency can mean a mixed infection or a contaminated sample.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is an allele frequency of 0.75, the cut-off nf-core/viralrecon documents for variants integrated into the consensus genome of its long variant table.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/viralrecon/master/docs/output.md
  kind: manhattan
  config:
    score_threshold: 0.75
    score_kind: Allele frequency
    color_by_columns:
    - EFFECT
    - sample
    default_color_by: EFFECT
    top_n_labels: 5
  roles:
    chr: CHROM
    pos: POS
    score: AF
    feature: GENE

- component: figure
  title: Allele frequency distribution
  description: |-
    Each bar counts the variants in a range of allele frequency, coloured by predicted effect. It answers how the variants split between minor and near-fixed.
    How to read: a peak at 1 holds the changes present in all reads, and a spread at lower frequencies holds minor variants. A peak near 0.5 can mean a mixed sample.
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: AF
    color: EFFECT
    labels:
      AF: Allele frequency
      EFFECT: Predicted effect

- component: card
  title: Variant calls
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of variant calls across all samples, with the number of distinct genome positions beside it, and the bars rank the genes carrying most of them. It answers how much variation there is and where.
    How to read: a large gap between calls and positions means the same positions are shared by many samples, as expected for a lineage. A gene leading the ranking is a hotspot or a long gene.
  column: POS
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: GENE
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: variant calls, by gene
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Distinct variant positions
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct genome positions with a variant, and the bar shows how much of it the top genes hold. It answers whether variation is spread out or concentrated in a few genes.
    How to read: a large share in one or two genes marks a hotspot, or simply the longest genes. Compare with the lollipop tile.
  column: POS
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: concentration
  breakdown_col: GENE
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: share of positions in the top genes

- component: card
  title: Samples with variants
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of samples with at least one variant call, with the total number of calls beside it. It answers how many samples are in view and how many calls they carry.
    How to read: filter the dashboard to a group to compare how many samples and calls it holds.
  column: sample
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: vertical
  caption: samples and their variant calls

- component: card
  title: Protein changes
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct amino acid changes, leaving out variants with no protein change, with the number of calls beside it, and the bar splits the calls by predicted effect. It answers how much of the variation alters proteins.
    How to read: a bar dominated by synonymous changes means mostly silent variation. Missense and stop-gained shares mark the changes that could alter protein function.
  column: AA
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: EFFECT
  top_n_count: 3
  filter_expr: col('AA') != '.'
  caption: protein changes, by effect

- component: table
  title: Variant table
  description: |-
    One row is one variant call, with its position, alleles, depth, allele frequency, gene, protein change and predicted effect. It answers which exact variants a sample carries.
    How to read: Sort by allele frequency to separate fixed variants from minor ones, and by depth to spot calls with weak support. Look for high- impact effects at a high frequency. Select a row to filter the rest of the dashboard to its sample. It complements the frequency and effect tiles of the same output, which summarise these rows.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: sample

- component: advanced_viz
  id: variant_genome_view
  title: Variants along the genome
  description: |-
    Each point is a variant call at its genome position, with its allele frequency on the vertical axis, coloured by variant type (SNV, insertion or deletion). It answers where in the genome calls cluster and how many are near-fixed.
    How to read: points above the line are the high-frequency calls that would be integrated into a consensus, and points below it are minor variants. A stretch with many low-frequency calls can mean a mixed sample or a poorly covered region, so check the depth track.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is an allele frequency of 0.75, the cut-off nf-core/viralrecon documents for variants integrated into the consensus genome. iVar's own default minimum frequency to report a variant is 0.03, and viralrecon runs it at 0.25.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/viralrecon/master/docs/output.md and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/andersen-lab/ivar/master/docs/MANUAL.md
  kind: genome_view
  config:
    score_title: Allele frequency
    score_threshold: 0.75
  roles:
    chr: chrom
    pos: pos
    score: af
    feature: variant_key
    sample: genome_id
    category: variant_type

- component: advanced_viz
  id: af_vs_depth
  title: Allele frequency against depth
  description: |-
    Each point is a variant call: the read depth at its position on the horizontal axis and its allele frequency on the vertical axis, coloured by frequency class. It answers which calls rest on enough reads to be trusted.
    How to read: fixed calls sit at the top at any depth. Calls at low frequency and low depth, in the bottom left, are the least reliable because a handful of reads decides the frequency. Minor calls at high depth are credible intra-host variants.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is an allele frequency of 0.75, the cut-off nf-core/viralrecon documents for variants integrated into the consensus genome. The Fixed, Major and Minor classes (at least 0.9, 0.5 to 0.9 and under 0.5) are this table's own grouping, not published cut-offs. viralrecon calls variants from a depth of 10 reads by default, while iVar's own default minimum depth is 0.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/viralrecon/master/docs/output.md and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/andersen-lab/ivar/master/docs/MANUAL.md
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    log_x: true
    x_title: Total read depth at the position
    y_title: Allele frequency
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_value: 0.75
    reference_label: Consensus cut-off (0.75)
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    x: total_dp
    y: af
    label: variant_key
    color: frequency_class

- component: card
  id: pass_variants
  title: Variant calls
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of variant calls, with the number of distinct variants beside it, and the bar splits the calls by type. It answers how much variation was called and whether it is mostly substitutions or indels.
    How to read: a large gap between calls and distinct variants means the same variants recur across samples. A growing share of insertions or deletions is worth a look in the table, since they are more error-prone to call.
  column: variant_key
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: variant_type
  caption: calls, by variant type
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: frequency_classes
  title: Calls by frequency class
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of variant calls and the ring splits them into Fixed, Major and Minor by allele frequency. It answers how much of the variation is consensus-level and how much is intra-host diversity.
    How to read: a large Minor share means a mixed or diverse sample, or noise at low depth. The classes are this table's own grouping (at least 0.9, 0.5 to 0.9 and under 0.5), not a published cut-off.
  column: variant_key
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: frequency_class
  caption: calls, by frequency class

- component: figure
  title: Allele frequency distribution
  description: |-
    Each bar counts the variant calls in a range of allele frequency, coloured by frequency class. It answers how the calls divide between fixed changes and minor variants.
    How to read: a peak at 1 holds the consensus changes and a spread at low frequencies holds minor variants. A peak near 0.5 can mean a mixed sample.
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: af
    color: frequency_class
    labels:
      af: Allele frequency
      frequency_class: Frequency class

- component: interactive
  title: iVar filter verdict
  description: |-
    Filters the calls by iVar's verdict. iVar marks a call as PASS when the p-value of its Fisher's exact test is 0.05 or below, so the other calls are statistically weaker.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/andersen-lab/ivar/master/docs/MANUAL.md
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: filter

- component: table
  title: iVar variant table
  description: |-
    One row is one variant call, with its position, alleles, allele depths and frequency, p-value, iVar's verdict and the amino acid change when a GFF was given. It answers which exact variants each sample carries and whether iVar passed them.
    How to read: Sort by the allele frequency to separate fixed from minor variants, and by the p-value or the filter verdict to find doubtful calls. Look for calls that fail the filter or rest on a low depth. Select a row to filter the rest of the dashboard to its sample. It complements the frequency and variant-type tiles of the same output, which summarise these rows.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: genome_id
